items.stem: Explain why comparing the mean and variance of a set of count data helps to decide whether a Poisson model is suitable.
items.answer: For a Poisson distribution the mean and variance are equal, so if the sample mean and variance are close the model may be suitable; if they differ greatly it is not.

items.markingKey: B1 np > 5 / p not small; B1 normal approximation; B1 N(18, 12.6) [3]

items.stem: 0.8% of the light bulbs made in a factory are faulty. A box of 150 bulbs is chosen at random. Use a suitable approximation to find the probability that there are at most 1 faulty bulbs.

A seed company states that 0.8% of its seeds fail to germinate. A packet of 100 seeds is sown. Use a suitable approximation to find the probability that there are at least 2 seeds that fail to germinate. Justify your choice of approximation.

In a large population, 2% of people have a rare blood type. A random sample of 120 people is chosen. X is the number of people with the rare blood type. (a) State the exact distribution of X. (b) Explain why a Poisson distribution can be used as an approximation, stating its mean. (c) A larger sample of 360 is taken. Use a Poisson approximation to find the probability that it contains more than 8 people with the rare blood type.
The number of calls to a call centre in an hour has the distribution Po(31). Mateo uses N(31, 31) to find P(more than 38) as P(Y > 38). Explain the error and find the correct approximate probability.
items.answer: A continuity correction is needed: “more than 38” means X ≥ 39, so use P(Y > 38.5) = 0.0890.

items.stem: The number of cars passing a toll booth in a 10-minute period has the distribution Po(21). Ethan approximates P(more than 24) by standardising with (24.5 − 21) ÷ 21. Explain the error and find the correct approximate probability.
items.answer: The variance is 21, so the standard deviation is √21 = 4.58; dividing by 21 is wrong. P = 1 − Φ(0.764) = 0.223.
items.markingKey: B1 divide by √21; M1 standardise correctly; A1 0.223 [3]

items.stem: The number of particles emitted by a radioactive source in a minute has the distribution Po(72). Use a suitable approximation to find the probability that there are at most 68 in a minute.
items.markingKey: B1 N(72, 72); M1 continuity correction 68.5; M1 standardise (68.5 − 72)/√72 = −0.412; A1 0.340 [4]

items.stem: The number of cars passing a toll booth in a one-minute period has the distribution Po(4.5). (a) Find the probability that there are at most 1 in a one-minute period. (b) State the distribution of the number in a 8-minute period and explain why a normal approximation is appropriate.
